newsitem.title: USA: BASKETBALL-KENTUCKY NAMES GEORGIA'S TUBBY SMITH AS HEAD COACH.
newsitem.headline: BASKETBALL-KENTUCKY NAMES GEORGIA'S TUBBY SMITH AS HEAD COACH.

text.p: Tubby Smith landed one of the most prestigious and pressure-packed jobs in collegiate sports when he was named Monday to replace Rick Pitino as head basketball coach at the University of Kentucky.

The announcement came after Tubbs won the recommendation of the school's Athletic Association board. Smith, a former Kentucky assistant under Pitino, leaves the top job at Georgia for a five-year contract with Kentucky at undisclosed terms.

Smith, 46, becomes the first black coach at Kentucky, whose status as a top hoops power was established by Adolph Rupp, who retired as the most successful college coach ever but refused to recruit black players before relenting in the late 1960s.
"I hope I will be judged on the content of my character rather than the colour of my skin," said Smith. "A lot of people are interested and excited because I am a black coach."

Smith, whose son, G.G. Smith, is a player on the Georgia basketball team, earlier this year agreed with Georgia on a two-year contract extension worth approximately $780,000 per year through the 2002-03 season.
"It's tough whenever you leave a place," Smith said. "I know that this is a new challenge for me and my family."
Filling the shoes of Pitino, who left to take over the Boston Celtics for an astonishing 10-year, $70 million deal, will be no small task for Smith.
Pitino took Kentucky from probation to the 1996 NCAA Championship and had a return engagement in the NCAA Championship final this year before losing in overtime to Arizona.

Smith, who served as a Kentucky assistant under Pitino from 1989 to 1991, arrived in Georgia in 1995 to replace Hugh Durham. In his first season, the Bulldogs went 21-10 and reached the regional semifinals of the NCAA Tournament.
This season, Georgia went 24-9 but was upset by Chattanooga in the first round of the NCAA Tournament.

"I think we have absolutely chosen the very best candidate in the nation," said Kentucky president Dr. Charles T. Wethington, Jr. "In Tubby Smith, we truly have made a choice that we will all be happy with."
"It became apparent that Tubby had a fire in his belly to take this challenge on," Athletic Director C.M. Newton said.
"I am excited and delighted that Tubby is accepting the challenge. He was the only person that came to my mind that would be a candidate for this job."
Under Smith, the Wildcats are expected to play a similar system to the one installed by Pitino.

"We want to continue to play the same style," he said. "We played a similar style at Georgia. We like to run a matchup press and were one of the top teams in the league in opponents' field goal percentage."

After 12 years as an assistant at Virginia Commonwealth, South Carolina and Kentucky, Smith's first head coaching job came at Tulsa in 1991. In four years, he compiled a 79-43 mark. His overall record is 124-62.

"It's not overwhelming, it's every coach's dream," Smith said about taking the Kentucky job. "That's why you compete, so you can be the best. That's our goal, to be the best team in the country. That's been the goal everywhere I've coached."
